The clinical indicators for [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) in [[Danmark]] provide a comprehensive framework for evaluating the quality of cardiovascular care, from initial diagnostic procedures to long-term monitoring and adverse event tracking. These metrics are essential for assessing healthcare delivery across national and regional levels, ensuring that patients receive timely interventions and routine check-ups.

Diagnostic and routine monitoring indicators show high compliance rates across the country. For instance, [[Ekkokardiografi]] is tracked as a primary diagnostic tool (Indikator 2) for newly diagnosed patients, measuring the proportion who receive an echocardiogram between six months before and three months after their initial diagnosis date [^src2]. Routine blood monitoring is also highly effective; under [[Indikator 4b]], 93.9% of patients nationally (96,468 out of 102,690) received at least one annual S-creatinine measurement in 2022/23 [^src1]. Regional performance is similarly strong, with [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] achieving a 95.7% compliance rate (11,029 out of 11,526 patients) in 2023/24 [^src1].

The registry also closely tracks severe adverse outcomes within the first year of diagnosis. Between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2023, 3.2% of newly diagnosed patients nationally developed severe bleeding ([[Indikator 11]]), while 6.1% developed heart failure ([[Indikator 15]]) [^src3]. Supplementary analyses ([[Supplerende analyser 7]]) further noted that 2.14% of all prevalent atrial fibrillation patients experienced severe bleeding during this same period [^src3]. Regional variations are evident; for example, in [[Klynge VEST]], the rates for newly diagnosed patients were slightly higher, with 4.4% developing severe bleeding and 4.7% developing heart failure [^src3].

Patient demographics and risk stratification provide crucial context for these clinical outcomes. The average age of incident atrial fibrillation patients in Denmark is 74 years [^src4]. To evaluate stroke risk and guide anticoagulation therapy, the [[CHA2DS2-VASc]] scoring system is utilized. The national average score for incident patients is 1.75, and a significant majority—60.21%—present with a score of ≥2, indicating a clinically significant risk profile that typically warrants medical intervention [^src4].
